opening.name: Italian Game
opening.summary: The bishop aims at f7 while White builds a centre with c3 and d4, slowly and safely.

about.idea: Develop quickly, aim the bishop at f7, then prepare the d4 break with c3 while the king castles.
about.risks: Slow if White drifts; Black equalises with accurate play, so the plan matters more than the moves.
about.suits: Beginners who want natural moves, a safe king and chances to spring traps.

variations.name: Giuoco Piano
variations.intro: Black copies White with 3...Bc5; White builds the centre with c3 and d3.

variations.name: Traps to know
variations.intro: What to do when Black pins the knight too early.

giuoco-piano-main.name: Giuoco Piano: the quiet main line

note.text: Takes the centre and opens lines for the queen and the bishop on f1.
Develops a piece and attacks the e5 pawn, so Black must defend it.
Defends e5 with a piece and develops. Black never plays 2...Nf6 3.Nxe5 (the Stafford Gambit) or 3...Nd4 (the Blackburne Shilling): traps for beginners that lose against anyone who knows the answer.
Points the bishop at f7, the weakest square in Black's camp: at the start only the king defends it.
Copies White: the bishop eyes f2 and Black can castle soon. It also avoids 3...Nf6 4.Ng5, which asks a beginner for several exact moves.
Prepares d4. With a pawn on c3, White can take the centre and hit the bishop on c5 in one move.
Develops with an attack on e4, so White has to defend the pawn.
Guards the pawn on e4 and keeps the centre closed. White builds slowly first; the d4 break can wait until the pieces are ready.
Gives e5 a pawn to defend it and frees the c8 bishop.
Gets the king safe before the centre opens.
Castle now: the king is safe behind its pawns and the rook is ready for the centre.

Makes room on a7, so the bishop can step back there if White plays d4. It also stops Bb5 or Nb5 ideas.
Steps back out of reach of ...b5 and keeps the bishop on the diagonal that points at f7.
